stem.en: Glycerol is a three-carbon chain with a hydroxyl on every carbon. It is thick, sweet, and mixes with water in any amount. Kabir says "three hydroxyls is three times as sour as one". What is it?

text.en: Not sour at all. Hydroxyls love water but do not give up their hydrogen as an ion. Sourness needs a carboxyl. Three hydroxyls make it very water-loving and sticky, which is why it is thick.

feedback.en: Oxygen alone is not sourness. Vinegar's sour comes from the carboxyl's particular arrangement, which glycerol lacks.
The opposite. Three water-loving spots on a three-carbon chain leave no oily part to speak of.
Nitroglycerine is glycerol with a very different group hung on it. Glycerol itself is a food additive.

explanation.en: Read the groups. Hydroxyl means water-loving. Carboxyl means sour. Count which ones are present, not how many oxygens.
